 Watch: James Harden pours in 24 in first half as Cavaliers lead Pacers
 Originally posted on
 Ball Exclusives 
  | 
 Last updated Nov 20, 2026 9:00 PM ET
 Add us as a preferred source on Google
 James Harden carried the Cleveland Cavaliers through the first half against the Indiana Pacers on Friday night, scoring 24 points in 18 minutes. The NBA said it was his highest-scoring half as a Cavalier. 
 Harden went 8-of-14 from the field, 3-of-6 from three and 5-of-5 at the line, according to ESPN. He did most of it with step-backs: three of them from deep, including a 23-footer at 4:59 of the first quarter and a 24-footer at 4:57 of the second. He also drew a foul on a three for three free throws late in the first quarter.
 JAMES HARDEN JUST POSTED HIS HIGHEST-SCORING HALF AS A CAV 
 24 PTS
8-14 FGM
3-6 3PM pic.twitter.com/E1lqtCOgJ3 
 — NBA (@NBA) November 21, 2026 
 He was setting up teammates, too. Harden added five assists, three of them in the last 3:34 of the half, as Peyton Watson and Thomas Bryant hit threes off his passes. Cleveland was plus-11 with him on the floor. 
 It was still a one-point game at the break, with the Cavaliers up 62-61 in the NBA Cup East Group B matchup. Kelly Oubre Jr. led Indiana with 13 points, and Andrew Nembhard added 11. Cleveland came into the night 8-8, and Indiana 5-10. 
 The Ball Exclusives take
 This is the version of Harden Cleveland brought in for: step-back threes, trips to the line and the ball in his hands when the offense stalls. Donovan Mitchell went 2-of-7 in the half and the Cavs still led. If Harden can carry the scoring on nights like that, Cleveland has two players who can take over a game, and that is a problem for the East.
